thread.title: Earnings worries weigh on Asian markets

author: morningstar.com
title: Earnings worries weigh on Asian markets
text:
By Lucy Craymer
Samsung falls on outlook uncertainty; AMA, Nomura drag Nikkei
Stock indexes in Japan and South Korea saw earnings-related hits early Friday, with Samsung Electronics falling 3% following rival and customer Apple's latest-quarter results.
Apple (AAPL) reported a slight drop in sales to end 2017 and give a downbeat revenue forecast for this quarter. But shares still rose 3.4% in after-hours trading as overall results beat expectations and because the stock's performance had been lackluster for several months on worries about demand for the iPhone X.
Samsung (005930.SE) , which has its own line of smartphones but also makes various phone components including chips and screens, fell 3%. "The market is concerned about the uncertainty" surrounding its outlook, said S.K. Kim, an analyst at Daiwa Capital Markets. Chip maker SK Hynix (000660.SE) dropped 1.5%, helping push the Kospi index down 1.1%.
Japan's Nikkei slid 1.3% as it was hit by earnings-related news after jumping 1.7% Thursday. Airline ANA (9202.TO) and investment bank Nomura (8604.TO) both reported results after the bell, and their shares were down 3.6% and 2.5% respectively.
As for Thursday's jump, "I think the market got carried away" since some other indexes were down, said Michael McCarthy, CMC Markets' chief market strategist in Australia.
China stocks fell a further 1% after Thursday's declines of at least that much while stock benchmarks in Hong Kong and Taiwan dropped 0.5%.
But Australia's S&P/ASX 200 climbed 0.4% on a 1.8% jump in the energy sector, putting that group on pace for its best day in three months.
Oil futures were higher with the U.S. benchmark up 0.6% at $66.17 a barrel, poised to notch a fresh three-year settlement high. ANZ Bank said the market's focus has returned to the positive macroeconomic backdrop, looking past record levels for U.S. oil production.
Some investors were likely sidelined ahead of Friday's U.S. jobs report and continued gains in government-debt yields. The 10-year Treasury yield nearly reached 2.8% in Asian trading and was at four-year highs.
"Equity markets globally are becoming aware that bond yields are increasing, and ultimately that means scope for rate hikes" and stimulus efforts unwinding, said Stuart Ive, senior client manager at OM Financial. "These moves in the bond market might start to get investors a bit twitchy."
Bitcoin prices remain below $9,000, according to CoinDesk, after first breaching that level in Thursday afternoon U.S. trading for the first time in more than two months. Prices are 14% below day-earlier levels for the volatile cryptocurrency.
-Lucy Craymer ; 01-18 2219ET
